H10: the safety check, the bidding and the radio traffic of Lunar ATC fit a flight-class computer (measured CPU time, memory and bytes per robot-hour, scaled to a reference radiation-tolerant processor with a stated factor) and a 16 kbit/s-class link for 20 robots (PREREG change 1)

classes.BASE: the base computer at the habitat (reservation table, auction, ledger)
classes.lander: radio unit and landing-announcement part only (PREREG change 7); not sized here

laptop.processor: Intel Core i5-10500H (6 cores, 2.5 GHz base, 4.5 GHz turbo)
laptop.benchmark_note: Assumed: 4.5 GHz turbo (Intel spec) x 6.0 CoreMark/MHz (typical for this core generation; no published CoreMark for this chip found), range 4-7 CoreMark/MHz

flight.processor: Frontgrade Gaisler GR740 (rad-hard quad-core LEON4FT, 250 MHz)
flight.source: Cobham Gaisler, GR740 benchmark results, ESA DSP Day 2016: 1.97 CoreMark/MHz/core x 250 MHz; https://indico.esa.int/event/102/contributions/62/ ; product brief: https://download.gaisler.com/products/gr740/doc/Product%20Brief_GR740_20230908_rev1.pdf
flight.memory_flag: Assumed: SDRAM of a typical GR740 single-board computer
flight.factor_note: laptop CoreMark per core / flight CoreMark per core; the measured times are Python + numpy, a flight implementation in C would be faster, so the scaled times are an upper bound in that respect (Assumed)

radio.flag: Assumed (frequency as B-70's provisional 2.4 GHz; powers per class; worst hop = the mesh's 5 km range)

power_w.flag: Assumed: a GR740-class board (~4-5 W) plus the radio at the stated transmit power and duty; BASE adds the mast radio and storage

messages.flag: Assumed byte layouts (ids, times, positions as 32-bit values, headers 8 B); status at 1 Hz per R9

failover.regime: C_LEADER, message loss 0.1, 30 % load, 1x, one year

runs.regime: C_AUCTION, message loss 0.1, roads atc (15 % single-lane), dispatch to a fixed point
